title: CUBICS: Situation-aware performance estimation for safety-relevant ML components
abstract: arXiv:2608.16564v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Machine learning (ML) is a key technology driving innovation today, but ensuring ML safety remains a major challenge for safety-related applications. A promising idea is to build proven-in-use arguments from field data, e.g. by running ML components (MLCs) in shadow mode or within safety envelopes so that their outputs can be monitored as 'safe probes' without affecting safety. These probes can then be used to build a statistical argument about field performance in a Bayesian way. However, many Bayesian field-data approaches in safety engineering model failures as a simple Bernoulli (or binomial) process with a single global failure probability and i.i.d. trials, which is rarely adequate for MLCs whose performance depends strongly on context. Statistical evidence is also about coverage of relevant situations, including edge cases, and building a single integrated statistical model for the entire system is usually not feasible. To address

translated_title: CUBICS：面向安全相关机器学习组件的情境感知性能评估
translated_abstract: 机器学习（ML）是当今推动创新的关键技术，但确保ML安全性对安全相关应用仍是一个重大挑战。一个有前景的思路是利用现场数据构建“使用中证明”的论证，例如通过影子模式或安全包络运行ML组件（MLCs），使其输出可被监控为“安全探针”，而不影响安全性。这些探针随后可用于以贝叶斯方式构建关于现场性能的统计论证。然而，安全工程中许多贝叶斯现场数据方法将故障建模为简单的伯努利（或二项式）过程，具有单一全局故障概率和独立同分布试验，这通常不适用于性能强烈依赖上下文的MLCs。统计证据还涉及相关情境的覆盖，包括边缘案例，而为整个系统构建单一集成统计模型通常不可行。为解决此问题...
tldr: 本文提出CUBICS方法，通过情境感知的贝叶斯现场数据统计建模，解决安全相关机器学习组件性能评估中忽略上下文依赖和边缘案例覆盖的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes CUBICS, a situation-aware Bayesian field-data statistical modeling approach to address the issue of ignoring context dependence and edge-case coverage in performance evaluation of safety-relevant ML components.
